text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Arab foreign ministers to rocommend freezing normalisation with Israel.
- Yeltsin proposed to Netanyahu: "Russia will freeze missile deal with Iran in exchange for "proper compensation".
- Vote today in parliament on conversion law; one party in coalition to oppose, two others wavering.
- Prime Minister Netanyahu: Peace in "virtual collapse".
- Uproar over officer's slur against Ethiopian soldier.
- Politicians target end to direct elections.
- Treasury official: 1997 growth to be lower than three percent.
- Israel Corp. buys additional 17 percent stake in Israel Chemicals for 667 million shekels.
- United Mizrahi Bank net income up 17 percent last year.
- Police source: "Findings in Bar-On investigation are more severe than bus 300 scandal."
- Israel refuses to comment on report in Egyptian weekly that Israeli spy executed in Egypt two years ago.
- Palestinian woman in Tzurif village near Hebron says border policeman molested her.
- Cellcom loses 48.1 million shekels in fourth quarter of 1996.
